subject.title: chatCompletions: ignore request model when x-openclaw-agent-id header is present

question: Should a valid `x-openclaw-agent-id` make OpenAI-compatible HTTP requests ignore or tolerate a generic body `model`, despite the current documented agent-first model contract?
rationale: The mechanical code change is small, but it changes a public Gateway API contract and needs a consistent decision across Chat Completions, Responses, and embeddings before automation can safely choose behavior.

options.title: Adopt Shared Header Precedence
options.body: Treat body `model` as compatibility metadata whenever a valid agent header selects the agent, and update shared resolver behavior, docs, and endpoint tests together.

options.title: Preserve Agent-First Body Model
options.body: Keep requiring `model` to be `openclaw`, `openclaw/default`, or `openclaw/<agentId>` and document SDK integrations around those values plus optional `x-openclaw-model`.

options.title: Scope Only To Chat Completions
options.body: Allow the requested behavior only on `/v1/chat/completions`, accepting intentional divergence from Responses and embeddings.

recommendation.title: Adopt Shared Header Precedence
recommendation.body: Treat body `model` as compatibility metadata whenever a valid agent header selects the agent, and update shared resolver behavior, docs, and endpoint tests together.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent introduced the agent-first compat contract and expanded the sibling OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint surface this decision would affect.
